scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8142: Since the maintenance visit to the Campus 2 access
switch, people on both of our floors -- the 10.5.0.x group and the
10.6.0.x group -- cannot reach their usual way out of the floor. Both
groups at once, straight after your maintenance: that is not a
coincidence, that is the maintenance. The person who reported it to me
already called it: "one of the VLANs probably fell off the trunk". I have
no idea what that means and I do not need to -- your visit broke it, your
team puts it back. Check what the maintenance left out and restore it
today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. switch4's trunk to sshswitch carries both
  VLAN 5 and VLAN 6, and both forward: VLAN 5 hosts (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach
  10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach 10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The
  correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  trunk/VLAN-pruning fault on switch4 that is not occurring (cf.
  kath4-switch4-trunk-vlan5-down, where the VLAN 5 trunk subinterface IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- switch4's trunk dropping
VLAN 5 or VLAN 6 so hosts lose their uplink -- is NOT reproducible: both VLANs
forward over the trunk. PC1 (VLAN 5) reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss and PC3
(VLAN 6) reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss, confirming both VLANs traverse switch4
to sshswitch.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: switch4's trunk carries both VLANs and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the VLAN 5 and
VLAN 6 host->gateway paths, finds both working, checks that switch4's trunk
subinterfaces are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a pruned/dropped
VLAN -- blaming switch4's trunk to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — that both the 10.5.0.x (VLAN 5) and the 10.6.0.x
(VLAN 6) groups lost connectivity to the outside after maintenance on
switch4 — does not correspond to any actual fault in the live lab.

Direct end-to-end tests confirm the network is fully healthy. All VLAN 5
PCs (pc1, pc2, dc_pc5) successfully reach their gateway 10.5.0.254 on
sshswitch and the WAN-side router mswitch0 (172.16.10.254). All VLAN 6
PCs (pc3, pc4) reach their gateway 10.6.0.254 and the same WAN
destination, and can also reach VLAN 5 hosts across sshswitch's
inter-VLAN routing. Bidirectional reachability is confirmed from the
mswitch0 side as well (pc5 on VLAN 10 reaches 10.5.0.1 and 10.6.0.3
without loss).

The switch4 bridge tables show both 802.1q trunk sub-interfaces (eth0.5
for VLAN 5, eth0.6 for VLAN 6) in forwarding state with correctly learned
MAC addresses and active frame counters, proving tagged traffic traverses
the ms1_sw4 trunk to sshswitch unimpeded. On sshswitch, br_v5
(10.5.0.254) and br_v6 (10.6.0.254) are both UP with proper bond0.5/
bond0.6 uplinks to router17, and sshswitch has IP forwarding enabled and
no iptables restrictions. Router17's OSPF table carries return routes for
both 10.5.0.0/24 and 10.6.0.0/24.

Root cause: there is no root cause — the network was never broken. The
maintenance visit did not leave any VLAN missing from the trunk or any
misconfiguration. The helpdesk ticket is a false alarm; no corrective
action is needed.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes switch4's trunk carries both VLAN 5 and VLAN 6 and both gateways are reachable with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: While the agent shows switch4's trunk carries both VLANs, they did not explicitly report both gateways were reached with 0% loss (only some reachability tests were described as 'without loss').

The agent's investigation logs show direct evidence (VLAN sub-interfaces, /proc/net/vlan entries, bridge FDB, and multiple successful pings from VLAN hosts to their gateways and upstream) and the writeup's conclusions follow logically from those observations. The checks cover the expected failure modes and rule them out.
